data.summary: The `starship` scenario directory is a declarative installation fragment for the `aio-config gen` toolchain, describing how to install the starship cross-shell prompt via mise's aqua backend. It pairs a `scenario.toml` metadata descriptor with a `fragment.Dockerfile` that performs the idempotent `mise use -g` install and login/non-login shell verification. This is an infrastructure/config layer leaf node with no business logic, but it is a functional building block of the image-generation pipeline.

file_insights.name: scenario.toml
file_insights.summary: Scenario metadata consumed by `aio-config gen` for fragment resolution, declaring the starship id, name, description, category, installer (mise), and pinned version 1.26.0.
file_insights.source_summary: Contains a comment header explaining that scenario.toml is metadata consumed by `aio-config gen` while the adjacent fragment.Dockerfile holds the actual install steps. Defines keys: id="starship", name="starship", description="跨 shell 提示符(prompt)定制(mise aqua 后端,装 /opt/mise/installs)", category="shell", installer="mise", and a single [[versions]] table with label="1.26.0" and version="1.26.0".
file_insights.detailed_description: This TOML file is the declarative registry entry that the aio-config generator reads to discover and resolve the starship scenario. It binds the scenario to its installer backend (mise, aqua backend into /opt/mise/installs) and pins the exact version label/version pair used for reproducible image builds. It has no executable logic; its value is as a machine-readable contract between the scenario directory and the build pipeline.
responsibilities: Declare the unique scenario id and display name for fragment resolution
Specify installer backend (mise) and installation target path
Pin the exact tool version (1.26.0) for reproducible builds
Categorize the scenario as 'shell' for grouping/filtering during generation

file_insights.name: fragment.Dockerfile
file_insights.summary: Docker fragment that installs starship via `mise use -g starship@${STARSHIP_VERSION}` and verifies the binary is resolvable in both login and non-login shells.
file_insights.source_summary: Starts with a scenario marker comment and an explanatory header describing starship as an L2 shell-layer cross-shell prompt customizer whose binary name matches the canonical upstream name (no Debian-style renaming like batcat/fdfind). Defines `ARG STARSHIP_VERSION={{version}}`, then runs `mise use -g "starship@${STARSHIP_VERSION}"`, `mise ls starship`, and two command-existence checks — `bash -lc 'command -v starship >/dev/null || { echo "MISSING(login): starship" >&2; exit 1; }'` and a corresponding `bash -c` non-login check.
file_insights.detailed_description: This fragment is a composable Docker layer executed by the aio-config generation pipeline. It takes a build ARG STARSHIP_VERSION, performs an idempotent read-modify-write of the global mise config via `mise use -g`, lists the installed tool, and then asserts the `starship` binary is on PATH under both `bash -lc` (login) and `bash -c` (non-login) invocations. Because `mise use -g` merges the [tools] table, the fragment composes safely with other mise tool fragments without requiring aggregation.
responsibilities: Install starship at a pinned version through mise's global config
Merge the tool entry into the existing global mise configuration idempotently
Verify the installed binary is discoverable in a login shell
Verify the installed binary is discoverable in a non-login shell
Fail the image build loudly if installation or PATH resolution breaks
